as a library, this is a bit more low-level

tools

So that would be worth a look. If you know
that you'll be building agents, you could
also go for A framework specialized on
building agents though. The difference
between a framework and a library is
that a library is
more general, you could say. A framework has
more opinions, more clear guides or
structure you have to follow, and a bit less
flexibility for you. But the advantage of
using a framework like, for example, CrewAI,
which would be a very popular framework for
building AI agents,
is that you have less choices to make. You
have to wire up less
things. More works out of the box. And that,
of course, can be convenient. So it's
basically a trade-off. Do you buy into a
framework, so to say, and follow the
structure and the guides they give you? Or
do you prefer a more low-level self-built
solution like could have it with libraries
like the AI SDK?
CrewAI, as mentioned, is one example for a

building agents. Another example for such a

It is there to help you build agents and not
